<b>Den är gjord av tal.</b> En modell so: It is made of numbers. A model like Llama-3-8B consists of roughly 8 billion numbers, called weights or parameters. Together they take up 16 GB.
<b>Talen är inlärda.</b> Modellen har lä: The numbers are learned. The model has read enormous amounts of text and adjusted its numbers until it got good at guessing the next word. No one typed in the rules by hand.
<b>Den slår inte upp svar.</b> Det finns: It does not look up answers. There is no database of facts inside, only numbers that get added up. The knowledge is spread out across the numbers.
<b>Den skriver ett ord i taget.</b> Varj: It writes one word at a time. Each new word is appended to the text, and the model runs again to guess the next.
En språkmodell gör en enda sak: den giss: A language model does one thing only: it guesses which word comes next. Same idea as the word suggestions on your phone, just vastly bigger. Everything else, answering questions, writing code and reasoning, is built by making that guess over and over.
